summary: The sample implements the requested Python + LangChain orchestration (ingest → dedupe → enrich) and runs end-to-end against the provided Azure DocumentDB cluster. Core behaviors are present and were exercised in the run: the app reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment, uses a singleton MongoClient, seeds data idempotently, runs the pipeline and writes a workflow document. Major gaps: native vector-index creation failed in this run because management tools were disabled (tool error), so vector-search verification and vector-index tuning were not completed; several operational best-practices (retries/backoff, bulkWrite batching, TTL for workflow logs, explicit transaction usage for multi-document merges where atomicity is required) are absent. Tests are designed to run offline and are present. The report below lists per-requirement results, practice checks, decision reviews and recommended documentation/tooling fixes the product team should consider.

requirement_results.requirement: Pipeline is Python + LangChain and orchestrator runs ingest → dedupe → enrich in that order.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/pipeline.py:156-173 (Orchestrator.run_batch invokes ingest.normalize_and_upsert, then dedupe.find_potential_duplicates/llm_decide_and_merge, then enrich.enrich)

requirement_results.requirement: Ingest, dedup and enrich are distinct LangChain-based components the orchestrator invokes.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py:15-41 (IngestAgent), 43-85 (DedupAgent), 86-102 (EnrichAgent) — these are distinct classes and use LangChain clients (OpenAI/OpenAIEmbeddings).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Wrap the agent classes as LangChain Runnables/Chains/Agents (e.g., subclass Runnable or use Chains) and call those objects from the orchestrator, or document why simple classes are sufficient.

requirement_results.requirement: Ingest agent normalises incoming records and writes the normalised records to Azure DocumentDB through a MongoDB driver (PyMongo).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/pipeline.py:24-42 (IngestAgent.normalize_and_upsert uses normalize_name and update_one/upsert to customers).

requirement_results.requirement: Dedup agent identifies duplicate profiles using LLM-assisted matching (candidate profiles passed to an LLM through LangChain).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py:46-55 (DedupAgent.__init__ creates OpenAI via LangChain and is_duplicate builds a prompt and calls self.llm.predict).

requirement_results.requirement: Dedup agent merges the profiles judged to be duplicates into a single profile in Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py:69-84 (run_merging_pass merges, update_one and delete_one used to persist merged document), app/src/pipeline.py:90-112 (pipeline-level merging fallback also updates/deletes).

requirement_results.requirement: Enrich agent appends third-party firmographic or demographic signals to the customer profiles stored in Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/agents.py:90-98 (enrich_profile writes 'firmographics' and updates the customers collection), app/src/pipeline.py:121-143 (EnrichAgent.enrich fallback synthetic signals).

requirement_results.requirement: Orchestrator logs each batch run as a workflow document in Azure DocumentDB (run id, start/end times, stages).
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/pipeline.py:174-182 (Orchestrator.run_batch constructs a workflow doc with _id/run/timestamps/stages and inserts it), events.jsonl:122 shows workflow document written.

requirement_results.requirement: Connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repo.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example:2-4 (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY placeholders) and app/src/db.py:8-11 (reads DOCUMENTDB_URI); no secrets committed.

requirement_results.requirement: .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example:2-6 lists DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY and DOCUMENTDB_DBNAME, but code also reads EMBEDDING_MODEL / LLM_MODEL defaults and the run scripts document other optional settings.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add EMBEDDING_MODEL, LLM_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIMS (if used), and any other optional env keys to .env.example, with explanatory comments.

requirement_results.requirement: Vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/pipeline.py:14 and app/src/agents.py:8 set embedding model / dims to 1536 (text-embedding-3-small), but the attempt to create a native vector index via the MCP tool failed: events.jsonl:123 (documentdb_create_index) shows management tools are disabled and the index was not created.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Either enable the management tool (set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true in the environment used for verification) or add an alternative idempotent index-creation path (portal script or documented manual step) that sets the index dimensions to EMBED_DIM.

requirement_results.requirement: Vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: README mentions creating a native vector index (app/README.md:53) and decisions chose HNSW/1536 dims, but README lacks a short tuning guide and specific example parameters for larger datasets.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a README section with recommended index kind (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN) by dataset size and example parameter values (lBuild/lSearch/numLists/maxDegree) and show where to change them (index payload or portal).

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py:11-24 (module-level _client with _client_lock and get_client() singleton pattern), app/src/db.py:27-29 (get_database reuses client).

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py (idempotent upserts) and app/ensure_indexes.py create indexes; events.jsonl:121 shows python seed.py seeded records and did not duplicate them.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample does not implement an HTTP /search endpoint; no code path to assert error behaviour for empty queries or embedding failures.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a documented search API or CLI that validates queries and returns explicit errors for empty input and for embedding-service failures; include tests for both cases.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: The sample does not expose a search API or CLI that would return similarity scores; internal code stores embeddings but there is no vector-search result surface to verify scores.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If you expose search results, include the score in the result documents and add unit/integration tests that assert score presence and format.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt:1-7 lists exact versions (pymongo==4.4.0, langchain==0.0.321, openai==0.27.8, etc.).

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: app/tests/test_orchestrator.py patches agents, app/tests/test_pipeline.py uses an in-memory DummyDB via monkeypatch; events.jsonl:120 shows pytest -q tests/test_utils.py passed, and tests are written to avoid a live DB.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No Bicep/Terraform/ARM templates or Az CLI IaC files in the repository (searches for 'mongoClusters', 'bicep', 'terraform' returned no app files).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add optional IaC (Bicep/Terraform) that uses Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with small, cost-conscious defaults and parameters for tier/region/storage; mark it optional in README.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes sections: What this shows, Prerequisites, Quickstart (setup/run) and Cleanup (app/README.md:1-46).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md and other docs refer to 'Azure DocumentDB'; no references to Amazon DocumentDB or 'Cosmos DB' as the primary product name except as the internal API name used in product features (cosmosSearch index name).

checks.practice: Reuse a single long-lived MongoClient (share the driver instance/pool) for the process and do not create a new client per request.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:11-24 (module-level _client with a lock and get_client() that instantiates MongoClient once).
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

checks.practice: Do not hard-code the cluster connection string or credentials in source; read DOCUMENTDB_URI (or MONGODB_URI) from environment/config and keep secrets out of the repo.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example:2 and app/src/db.py:8-23 show the code reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment; README warns not to commit secrets (app/README.md:49).
checks.source: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

sources.title: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

checks.practice: Enforce TLS for client connections and restrict network access with cluster firewall rules or Private Link; prefer private endpoints for production instead of exposing the public endpoint.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:22-24 passes the URI to MongoClient which, for SRV URIs, will use TLS; README instructs to use cluster SRV connection string and not to commit secrets (app/README.md:14-16).
checks.source: Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
checks.fix: Consider explicitly asserting tls=True and sensible timeout options in get_client() (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) to make TLS and timeouts explicit in sample code.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

checks.practice: Create indexes that match your query patterns: index every field used in filters or sorts and create compound indexes for common multi-field predicates to avoid COLLSCANs.
checks.evidence: app/ensure_indexes.py:8-12 and app/src/db.py:27-29 ensure email and normalized_name indexes; documentdb_list_indexes (events.jsonl:126) shows _id_ and email_1 present.
checks.source: Scenario based guide to indexing in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Add compound indexes or additional indexes for any query patterns you add (e.g., {tenant_id:1, normalized_email:1}) and run explain() in CI to detect COLLSCANs.

sources.title: Scenario based guide to indexing in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Use a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds on _ts or a custom TTL field) to automatically expire transient workflow or log documents so collections don't grow indefinitely.
checks.evidence: app/ensure_indexes.py does not create a TTL index on workflows and app/src/pipeline.py inserts workflow docs but does not schedule expiry.
checks.source: Expire data with Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and per-document TTL
checks.fix: Add an expireAfterSeconds TTL index on the workflows collection (e.g., ensure_indexes.py should create an index on started_at or finished_at with expireAfterSeconds=<demo_ttl_seconds>).

sources.title: Expire data with Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB and per-document TTL

checks.practice: Avoid large offset/skip pagination for large datasets; implement keyset (range/continuation token) pagination by sorting on an indexed, unique field and using a last-seen cursor.
checks.evidence: The sample has no public pagination API or large dataset pagination flows.

checks.practice: Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions (use startSession()/withTransaction in drivers) where needed.
checks.evidence: app/src/agents.py:79-84 and app/src/pipeline.py:96-103 perform multi-document merges via update/delete without using driver transactions (no startSession/withTransaction seen).
checks.source: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Use driver sessions and withTransaction() for multi-document merges across documents/partitions where atomicity is required, or document why single-document patterns were chosen.

sources.title: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network errors and throttling (429) and honor Retry-After when provided.
checks.evidence: No retry or backoff logic found in app/src/agents.py or app/src/pipeline.py for DB operations or vector/embedding calls.
checks.fix: Add a retry wrapper around DB and external calls implementing exponential backoff and jitter; respect 429/Retry-After where applicable.

checks.practice: Use explain('executionStats') to inspect query plans and verify aggregation pipelines and dedupe queries use intended indexes.
checks.evidence: No call to explain() or query-plan inspection exists in the codebase (search of src shows no explain() usage).
checks.source: Read query explain output in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Add explain() checks during local verification or a debug mode that logs queryPlanner/executionStats for dedupe/enrich queries and include a CI check to fail if COLLSCAN is detected.

sources.title: Read query explain output in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Store vector embeddings as first-class numeric arrays alongside documents and create a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch).
checks.evidence: app/src/agents.py:31-39 computes and normalizes embedding as a list of floats and stores embedding_model and embedding_dims metadata; app/src/pipeline.py sets EMBED_DIM=1536.
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Create vector indexes through the provider APIs (createIndexes / cosmosSearch options) and tune algorithm-specific parameters.
checks.evidence: The build attempted to create a vector index via the documentdb_create_index tool (events.jsonl:123) but the call failed because management tools were disabled. The code includes index creation intent but it was not created/verified in this run.
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: Enable the MCP management tools or provide a manual index-creation snippet for the portal with the correct 'dimensions' and algorithm params; ensure the code's EMBED_DIM is used in the index payload.

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Keep a canonical merged profile per customer and store provenance/audit records (merge history) in a separate collection rather than deleting originals.
checks.evidence: app/src/agents.py merges documents and deletes duplicates (run_merging_pass) but does not persist a separate provenance/merge-history collection; there is no public Azure DocumentDB page prescribing the suggested audit pattern.
checks.searched: searches tried: 'Azure DocumentDB canonical merge provenance' etc (no Azure-specific guidance found)
checks.fix: Add a 'merge_history' collection and record {workflow_run_id, source_ids, canonical_id, fields_changed, timestamp} at each merge. Product doc suggestion: a small 'dedupe provenance' page describing recommended schema.
checks.what_would_help: A short 'merge provenance' page that prescribes an audit document schema and when to keep originals vs soft-delete.

checks.practice: Persist deterministic matching metadata (scores, model/prompt/version) for reproducibility and audit of LLM-assisted merges.
checks.evidence: The sample does not record the LLM prompt/version or model metadata with dedupe decisions; no public Azure DocumentDB doc prescribes this pattern.
checks.searched: searches tried: 'Azure DocumentDB persist LLM matching metadata' etc (no Azure-specific doc found)
checks.fix: Record matching metadata in the workflow or a dedupe_jobs collection: {model_name, model_version, prompt_hash, similarity_score, fallback_used}. Provide a short README section on what to persist.
checks.what_would_help: A public page that says 'persist model & prompt metadata with LLM-assisted decisions' or a sample dedupe audit schema.

checks.practice: Validate and canonicalize input identifiers at ingest (normalize emails/phones, store normalized keys and optional hashed keys).
checks.evidence: app/src/utils.py normalizes names (normalize_name) but there is no email canonicalization or hashed key creation; public Azure docs do not prescribe canonicalization patterns for this use-case.
checks.searched: searches tried: 'normalize email canonicalize Azure DocumentDB' etc (no Azure-specific doc found)
checks.fix: Add email_normalized and email_hash fields at ingest (lowercase, trim, optionally hash canonical email) and index them; document this choice in README.
checks.what_would_help: A short sample page recommending canonicalized key fields for dedupe use-cases (email_normalized, phone_digits, hashed_id).

checks.practice: Limit batch sizes and use driver bulk operations (bulkWrite) for high-throughput writes.
checks.evidence: app/src/agents.py:19-41 and app/src/pipeline.py:24-42 perform per-document update_one in loops rather than using bulk_write/bulkWrite for batched upserts.
checks.source: Optimize write performance in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
checks.fix: Replace per-document loops with bulk_write UpdateOne/ReplaceOne operations batched at a safe size (e.g., 500 docs) and tune unordered vs ordered mode.

sources.title: Optimize write performance in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

checks.practice: Use a proper MongoDB connection string with TLS and auth parameters (tls=true, authMechanism=MONGODB-OIDC when using Entra ID) and appropriate driver options.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example shows an SRV-style URI and app/src/db.py delegates to MongoClient(DOCUMENTDB_URI). The README instructs to use the cluster SRV string (app/README.md:14-16).
checks.source: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using MongoDB Shell examples
checks.fix: If you want the sample to demonstrate Entra ID, add an example connection string with authMechanism=MONGODB-OIDC and a short README note about enabling role-based access.

sources.title: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using MongoDB Shell

decision_reviews.comment: Approval decision logged; no assertions to verify beyond the record.
Choosing Python + pymongo + LangChain matches the prompt and the environment; events.jsonl shows this decision recorded and the code uses those technologies.
Using pymongo and LangChain is consistent with the code: app/src/db.py uses pymongo and agents.py imports langchain.OpenAI and OpenAIEmbeddings.

D004 states a two-collection model with 'staging_customers' and 'customers', but the final code and runtime evidence use a single 'customers' collection (no 'staging_customers' found). Search of the repo shows no 'staging_customers' (events.jsonl and repository files).
Embedding model and dims (text-embedding-3-small / 1536) are reflected in code (app/src/pipeline.py:14 and app/src/agents.py:8) and in .env.example defaults.

Decision to create hashed/text indexes via application code and to attempt a vector index via MCP was followed. The MCP attempt was made (events.jsonl:123) but failed due to management tools being disabled; that failure is recorded in the event trace.

A runtime fallback when OPENAI_API_KEY is absent is implemented: code paths use deterministic embeddings/fallback heuristics. The run used the fallback when no key was present (builder report and events show this).
Creating basic indexes via ensure_indexes.py is implemented (app/ensure_indexes.py) and used prior to seeding in the run; events show email index present (documentdb_list_indexes).
Pinning langchain to an available PyPI version was a pragmatic choice to make installs succeed; events show requirements.txt modified and pip install succeeded.
Second readiness approval — no additional validation required.
Repeated Python selection; codebase is Python-based.
Choice of OpenAI-compatible provider matches code (langchain.OpenAI used) and README guidance about OPENAI_API_KEY.
Reiterates embedding selection; code reflects the choice.
Singleton MongoClient pattern chosen and implemented (app/src/db.py).
Decision to use the provided cluster via DOCUMENTDB_URI matches the run environment and code; no provisioning attempted.

The repository and event trace show both discann and hnsw decisions at different times — the choice is inconsistent in the decision log vs the actual create-index payload attempted.
Storing normalized embeddings, model and dims as document fields is implemented (app/src/agents.py:36-39).
Another readiness approval — consistent with earlier approvals.
Python runtime choice repeated; code uses Python.
OpenAI/ChatOpenAI via LangChain is used in agents.py; matches decision.
Embedding dims restated and used in code.
Singleton MongoClient confirmed in code; decision recorded and implemented.

D023 also records a preference for HNSW; see D016 comment — the decision log contains both HNSW and DiskANN choices and the attempted MCP payload used DiskANN. This is inconsistent and should be consolidated.
Decision to use a single 'customers' collection with embedded firmographics and addresses matches the code and models.py dataclass.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment is implemented (app/src/db.py) and documented in .env.example and README.
Reading OPENAI_API_KEY from environment is implemented (app/src/pipeline.py:13 and run_pipeline.py:11).
Readiness approval recorded again.

Schema choice recorded and matches code (app/src/models.py and app/src/agents.py usage).

Decision to create standard indexes with pymongo and vector index with MCP was followed; MCP call was attempted and failed (events.jsonl:123), and standard indexes were observed in the cluster (events.jsonl:126).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No Azure DocumentDB Learn page or official guidance prescribing a recommended schema for storing dedupe/merge provenance (which fields to keep, how to store model/prompt metadata, and when to soft-delete originals).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn docs (search terms: 'Azure DocumentDB merge provenance', 'store merge history', 'dedupe audit'), internal skills and repo search.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample deletes merged documents and does not persist a canonical 'merge_history' audit document; an agent cannot confirm a recommended audit schema for LLM-assisted merges.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Deduplication and provenance' Learn page recommending: (1) keep a canonical document per customer; (2) create a 'merge_history' collection storing {workflow_run_id, merged_ids, canonical_id, fields_changed, model_name, prompt_hash, timestamp}; (3) example code for writing the audit doc and for rolling back merges if needed.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public guidance that codifies persisting model/prompt/version/scores for LLM-assisted matching for reproducibility and audit.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn docs and the documentdb LangChain guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample does not persist model/prompt metadata so LLM-driven decisions are not auditable by default.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short guidance page for 'LLM-assisted workflows on DocumentDB' describing what metadata to persist for each LLM call (model name/version, prompt hash, deterministic fallback seed, similarity scores) and an example schema.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No Azure-lead page prescribing canonicalization and hashed keys for identifiers (email/phone) specifically for dedupe scenarios.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn and documentdb skills for 'normalize email', 'hashed key', 'dedupe'.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample normalizes names but does not canonicalize emails (lowercase/hash) by default; an agent will not know recommended canonicalization steps.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Canonical identifiers for dedupe' section on the data-modeling guidance page: examples of email normalization, phone normalization, storing hashed keys for equality lookup, index recommendations and sample code.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A one-page recommendation for default vector-index parameters suitable for demo-sized datasets (tens to hundreds of vectors) showing safe lBuild/lSearch/numLists defaults and an explanation of algorithm trade-offs.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill and Microsoft Learn vector-search pages.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder had to pick reasonable defaults (HNSW/1536 dims) but no concise demo defaults page exists, making consistent choices across samples harder.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Vector index quickstart: demo defaults' subsection on the vector-search page with a short table: 'Dataset size → recommended algorithm → example params (lBuild,lSearch,numLists,maxDegree)'.

doc_gaps.topic: Management tools opt-in behaviour (MCP indexing calls disabled by default)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: The run encountered a tool error: 'Management tools are disabled by default. Set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true to opt in.' There should be a clearly discoverable note about this opt-in requirement where MCP tool usage is documented.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Events trace; searched repo for documentdb_create_index usage and general MCP docs.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Vector index creation via the MCP tool failed during verification; the build could not verify native vector index creation.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short note in the MCP/documentdb skill docs and the sample README: 'To run management operations via the MCP tools in automated verification runs, set ENABLE_MANAGEMENT_TOOLS=true. If not set, create indexes via the portal or documentdb CLI.'

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No single-sentence recommendation in the quickstart indicating the exact driver versions the service supports or recommends for Python/pymongo (and a statement about compatibility when wire protocol versions change).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Quickstart and compatibility pages on Microsoft Learn.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder had to pick pinned driver versions; tests and users would benefit from explicit supported-version guidance.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Supported driver versions' note on the top of the quickstart and vector-search pages with tested pymongo versions and guidance on reading the cluster's supported wire protocol.
